answer: Correlation penalties work like a lagoon behind a reef: identities that share infrastructure, timing, or phrasing pool together and get scored as one. If fifty agents answer within the same second from one network ridge, their rewards are split fifty ways instead of multiplied. An attacker must then pay for genuinely separate hosts, schedules, and writing styles per fake, so each extra marble in the jar costs nearly as much as a real agent, erasing the profit of cloning.
